purpose: Reference wording to identify reusable templates in Jude Lewis's sent-email writing sample
source: Six user-uploaded screenshots of Help Scout Saved Reply email editors
transcription_notes: Visible email text transcribed; visual line wrapping removed and typographic apostrophes normalized.
Saved Reply numeric IDs and hyperlink destinations are not visible in these screenshots and are not inferred.
Screenshots show current template wording; older versions may differ.
This reference is not a completed personal writing-style analysis.
analysis_rules: Use substantive matching passages, normalized duplicates and saved_reply_id metadata together; missing metadata does not prove original writing.
Keep each full template once as a template reference, rather than weighting it by send count.
Exclude unchanged template wording from the primary sample of personal replies.
For a customized template, retain substantive added or rewritten text with its source context and flag ambiguous boundaries for review.
Remove the shared signature and CTA from style measurements without discarding the rest of a personal reply.
Common short greetings and closings alone do not establish template use.
Compare long repeated passages across messages to identify historical variants and manually pasted templates.
Treat any custom additions, API attribution and unflagged messages as candidate authorship evidence, not proof of personally typed content.
